nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Co(OH)2
nodes.procedure: The nickel foam (10×20×1.5 mm) was sequentially washed with dilute HCl (1 M), ethanol, and deionized water (each for 10 min) to remove surficial oxides and contaminants. The electrosynthesis of Co(OH)2 nanosheet array was carried out in a three-electrodes setup, using saturated calomel electrode (SCE) and Pt foil as reference and counter electrodes respectively. The growth of Co(OH)2 nanosheets was performed at constant potential -1.0 V vs. SCE in aqueous Co(NO3)2 (0.15 M) electrolyte for 300 seconds. The potentiostatic deposition was carried out at a potential of -1.0 V vs. SCE. The resulting Co(OH)2 nanosheet array was withdrawn and rinsed thoroughly with ethanol and distilled water.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of Co(OH)2 nanosheets. The nickel foam (10×20×1.5 mm) was sequentially washed... rinsed thoroughly with ethanol and distilled water.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Au NPs
nodes.procedure: The electrochemical deposition of Au NPs onto Co(OH)2 was carried out in a three-electrode configuration as above described. Specifically, Au NPs were deposited on Co(OH)2 by stepping the potential to -0.6 V vs. SCE for 10 s, followed by stepping back to -0.2 V vs. SCE for 10 s for three cycles, using aqueous electrolyte with 0.1 M NaCl and 5 mM HAuCl4.

nodes.name: Electrochemical oxidation to CoOOH
nodes.procedure: The Au/CoOOH was obtained from the as-prepared Au/Co(OH)2 via a simple cyclic voltammetry (CV) method in a three-electrode configuration, using Ag/AgCl (with saturated KCl) and Pt foil as the reference and counter electrodes respectively. The electrochemical oxidization process was performed at a scan rate of 100 mV s^-1 from 0 V to 0.8 V vs. Ag/AgCl for approximately 20 cycles in 1 M KOH solution.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows CoOOH nanosheets with average thickness of ~10 nm and diameter of 200-300 nm, vertical on Ni foam with array structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) images (Fig. 3a) show that the CoOOH nanosheets (with an average thickness of ∼10 nm and diameter of 200−300 nm) are vertical on Ni foam with array structure.

properties.description: High-magnification SEM image showing nanostructured surface with dense, interconnected nanofiber-like morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals Au NPs well dispersed on CoOOH nanosheets with average diameter of 4.3 nm; individual Au NP shows fringe distance of 0.203 nm matching (200) plane of fcc Au.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) images reveal that Au NPs are well dispersed on CoOOH nanosheets (Fig. 3b and Supplementary Fig. 15) with average diameter of 4.3 nm (Fig. 3c). The HRTEM image of an individual Au nanoparticle displays a fringe distance of 0.203 nm (Fig. 3b; inset), closely matching the (200) plane of face-centered-cubic Au.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD reveals γ-CoOOH phase with (003) and (006) reflections at 12.9° and 26.2°; Au (111) peak at 38.2° observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis of Au/CoOOH reveals a γ-CoOOH phase with typical (003) and (006) reflections at 12.9° and 26.2°, which is electrochemically transformed from its precursor, α-Co(OH)₂ (Fig. 3d and Supplementary Fig. 16). The reflection peak at 2θ = 38.2° for both Au/Co(OH)₂ and Au/CoOOH can be attributed to Au (111).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES shows Au mass loading of 11.3 wt% on CoOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) shows that the mass loading of Au on CoOOH is 11.3 wt% (Supplementary Table 3).

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ FTIR shows stronger benzyl alcohol adsorption on Au/CoOOH after 15 min He purging compared to Au and CoOOH alone; bands at 1455, 1435, 1418 cm⁻¹ indicate Au-benzene ring interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After 15 min of He purging, the signal of adsorbed benzyl alcohol on Au/CoOOH remains intense, much higher than that on Au and CoOOH, indicating a stronger interaction exists between benzyl alcohol and Au/CoOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EQCM shows more negative frequency shift for benzyl alcohol adsorption on Au/CoOOH than on Au, indicating promoted adsorption at the interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The initial frequency of Au/CoOOH after adding benzyl alcohol shows more negative shift than that of Au (blue curve in Fig. 4b), indicating that the adsorption of benzyl alcohol is promoted over Au/CoOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Au atoms at Au/CoOOH interface are more electron-deficient than in pure Au due to electron transfer from Au to CoOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, according to the Hirshfeld charge analysis, there is electron transferring from Au to CoOOH, giving rise to Au atoms in Au/CoOOH interface being more electron-deficient than those in pure Au (Supplementary Fig. 20), matching with the X-ray photoelectron spectra (XPS) results (Supplementary Fig. 21).

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Au L₃-edge EXAFS shows reversible Au oxidation/reduction; Au-O bond appears during operation and decreases during potential OFF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The reduction of Au oxide was confirmed by Fourier-transform Au L₃-edge EXAFS spectra (Fig. 6b), in which the Au−O signal was significantly decreased at potential OFF.
